text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Top religious figure Fethullah Gulen, known as Fethullah Hoja, who owns hundreds companies, schools, private teaching centres and student housing, is gearing up to flood the finance sector with enormous cash supplies.
- Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller denies calling on Iraqi president Saddam Hussein to enter Iraq, as reported in the New York Times over the weekend.
- Turkey's Kurdish rebels paid Tehran $5 million to buy a big guerrilla camp in Iran near its border with Turkey.

- An international draft contract on the distribution of Turkey's water resources -- an issue of contention between Turkey and its downstream neighbours -- will be discussed by the United Nations in October.
- The leader of the main opposition says in an interview how he plans to bring down the Islamist-led government.
- Foreign ministry spokesman Omer Akbel says the U.S.-led allied air force stationed in Turkey to protect Iraqi Kurds has lost its function and calls for a reviewing.
- Bussinesmen's grouping TUSIAD says Turkey has the potential to overcome its economic problems.
- Istanbul's Islamist mayor Tayyip Erdogan says he believes Tehran when it denies giving support to the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK).
- Civil servants will be given the right to form unions if they give up demands for the right to go on strike.
